433. Maximal Palindrome from Lists

Problem Statement:
You are given two lists of N strings each .You have to find the maximal palindrome from the two lists

The maximal palindrome is constructed as follows

Take a suffix of any string in the first list. Take a matching prefix for the reversed suffix picked from the first list in from the second list. Concatenate them and you have a palindrome.

Out of all the possible palindromes find the maximal palindrome i.e the one with the maximum size.

For example :

Consider the two lists as follows:

List1: [ abcd , efgh , hhjsgh , kkjk]

List2: [ bbng , dcnn , llolk , iiii ]

The answer is “cddn” constructed as follows:

abcd -> pick cd as suffix

dcnn-> pick dc as prefix

Concatenating them we get the palindrome: cddc Which is maximal from all possible palindromes constructed by appending a suffix from the first list and a prefix from the second list

If there are multiple answers print the lexicographically smallest one (i.e the one that comes first when they are written in alphabetical order)
input_spec:
First line contains a single integer N ,M - no of strings in each list
The next N lines contain a single string each describing the contents of the first list
The next M lines contain a single string each describing the contents of the second list
output_spec: The output must consist of a single line . Print the maximal palindrome possible or if no maximal palindrome is possible display “No maximal palindrome”
